newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 4.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Vice-chairman of the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) and Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec told Czech Television that Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus did not inform him of the letter from the IMF which proposed to approve certain measures reacting to the economic situation.

- Lockheed Martin, manufacturer of F-16 fighter aircrafts, authorised W.B. Zimmerman, a senior member of its management, to coordinate all activities connected with selling these aircrafts to the Czech Army.

- Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini met with Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus yesterday and said he still considers the Czech Republic one of the most successful reform countries and supports its entry into the EU and NATO.

- The Civic Democratic Party (ODS) proposed yesterday to immediately have a confidence vote for the cabinet in parliament, and it obtained the support of all cabinet parties. The Social Democrats (CSSD) first want a vote to be held on their proposal for the cabinet to resign.

PRAVO - Interest in placing money into short-term time deposits of up to two weeks, which have annual interest rates of more than 30 percent at most banks, increased further on Tuesday, but some banks, due to such high demand, closed access to the deposits.

- The new Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said yesterday that budget cuts of 70 billion crowns are unrealistic. The cabinet should present a new budget within a few weeks. Pilip considers it most important to cooperate with the central bank.
- Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka said yesterday that the circle of people who receive state aid should get smaller so those who really need it will receive more.

- After meeting with the chairman of the Czech-Moravian union federation, Richard Falbr, Deputy Prime Minister and leader of KDU-CSL, Josef Lux, proposed to discuss delaying some price deregulations due to restrictive measures which will affect citizens.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Slovak cabinet approved a quota on imports of Czech beer yesterday, probably 530,000 hectolitres of beer. It will meet with the customs union comprised of representatives from both countries today to discuss it.

- Foreign currency reserves in the Czech Republic amounted to $14.963 billion at the end of April, a month-on-month decline of 268 million dollars. The central bank's foreign currency reserves were $11.518 billion dollars, and commercial banks had $3.445 billion.

- Shareholders of Apollon Holding insist that their company, which was established last May from Agrobanka's first investment fund, was defrauded. In an open letter to ODS, ODA, KDU-CSL and CSSD, they blamed the case on a group of institutional shareholders of Agrobanka and Motoinvest.
- Nova Hut will obtain credit from the IFC and a consortium of domestic banks led by Komercni Banka. IFC will provide $250 million and domestic banks another $100 million.
- CEZ expects that demand for electricity will decrease and that its planned net profits of 6.1 billion crowns will be one billion crowns less than originally forecast.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Environment Minister Jiri Skalicky should become the new cabinet vice-chairman for the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), according to a proposal from the party's council.
- Former Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy decided to leave his post in parliament with his departure from the cabinet. His place will be taken by ecologist Milan Kyncl.

- After a meeting yesterday with Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny, the vice-chairman of the subcommittee for the future military strength of NATO, Portuguese Pedro Holstein Kampilho declared his support for the Czech Republic's entry into NATO.

- The Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting yesterday issued two fines amounting to one million crowns total to Ceska Televize for exceeding the limit of permitted advertisements and for broadcasting unannounced advertisements during sports broadcasts.

- While the largest health insurance company, Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna (VZP) had losses of three billion crowns, all 15 insurance companies had total losses of 1.8 billion crowns. The profits of smaller insurance companies stifled VZP's losses.
